review_notes: I read the whole file. It has two substantial proofs: `decompose_mul_mem_orderSymbolRelation` and `all_decompose_mem_orderSymbolRelation_of_mem_orderInitialIdeal`. The only shared pattern between them is the zero case. Each proves a component is zero, then closes with `exact Submodule.zero_mem _`. That is routine and too short to justify a shared lemma under this rubric. I also grepped the Stafford38 sources for similar uses of the graded-decomposition lemmas. `FibreConicalVanishingIdeal.coeff_fibreLinePolynomial_eq_eval_weightedHomogeneousComponent` and `ZeroSectionContainment.eval_zeroComponent` both use `MvPolynomial.induction_on`. Each splits into constant, add and `mul_X` cases and uses `coe_decompose_mul_of_right_mem_of_le`. That is a similar proof shape, but the goals differ (a polynomial coefficient versus an evaluation at a zero-section point), and the inductions are not interchangeable in any obvious way. I found no clean shared lemma that would improve the target file. I did not check every other use in the repository exhaustively.
